Gómez tapping, CAP models

Tap positions of 43 people on 16 one-bar drum loops (Gómez-Marín et al. 2026, Exp. 2), against the current CAP and two layer models.

Built 2026-11-17 from gomez-tapping-regression 674ab81. All pages

Giving each drum layer its own weight predicts where people tap better than the current CAP (R2 0.69 against 0.42, on loops left out of the fit).

Five loops

The layer weights match the observed taps on 0.94 of the steps of promisedland34 and on 0.50 of lovecantturnaround185. The other three compare the layer weights with the meter term and the current CAP.

Method
  • Tap share is the share of subjects who tapped on a step. A binomial regression fits it from each model's predictors on 15 loops and predicts the 16th (leave-one-pattern-out).
  • Grades cut that share at 0.5 and 0.67, weak accent from half the subjects, strong from two thirds.
  • Current CAP is the OHR rule on all onsets merged. Layer weights give each layer (kick, snare+clap, hats, other) its own weight on its onsets (rule R0). The meter term adds one weight for the beats and one for the other 8th steps.
  • Figure 1 picks, in this order, the loop where the layer weights match best, where they match worst, where the meter term gains most, where the current CAP beats the layer weights most and where it loses most. Each pick skips loops already taken.
  • The loops are rendered from the stimulus MIDIs with the TR-808 samples of the authors' repo, through their 8-stream reduction. Subjects heard TR-707, 808 and 909 samples, so timbres differ a little.
